item.title: Chrisean Rock’s Morgan Cook Fight Moves To March
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Chrisean Rock gets a March fight date against Morgan Cook as their November booking becomes a faceoff ahead of the bout.
item.content:encoded:
Chrisean Rock has a new date for her Morgan Cook fight, with the bout moving to March 20, 2027. The two women are still being advertised for a November 20 faceoff, rather than the fight previously promoted for that night.

The revised Official Celebrity Boxing announcement keeps Rock and Cook on the Philadelphia-area event’s bill. Jamie Campbell and Junior Butterbean now occupy the main-event spot on the promoter’s listing.

That show remains scheduled for Harrah’s Philadelphia Casino in Chester, Pennsylvania. Justina Valentine is still listed as host, with the event running from 7 P.M. to 11 P.M.

TrillerTV has also changed the air date at the top of its Rock-versus-Cook pay-per-view page to Saturday, March 20. Its promotional description still carries the old November date, while the promoter’s updated billing specifically advertises a faceoff for the March matchup.

Rock had been preparing to fight Cook during October, before the schedule changed. Cook, billed as Morgan “Victory,” remains the opponent on TrillerTV’s updated event page, which lists her record at 0-1.

The booking follows a year in which Rock moved from celebrity boxing into a sanctioned professional contest. She signed with Damon Feldman’s XRumble operation in January, then faced Zenith Zion in April at the same Pennsylvania casino.

Rock won that crossover bout by split decision, but it did not count toward her professional record. Her next appearance took her back to Baltimore, where she had trained with Calvin Ford. Ford is known for his work with Gervonta Davis.

In September, she stopped Ku’Shiyah Williams in the second round of her professional debut. Both fighters entered without a pro record, and Rock left with her first sanctioned victory. The referee halted the scheduled four-round contest after Williams absorbed a series of punches and could no longer answer Rock’s pressure effectively.

That Baltimore fight was staged at the Hyatt Regency Inner Harbor on Skyy Myles Promotions’ “The Supper” card, carried on BLK Prime pay-per-view. TrillerTV’s current marketing counts her two boxing wins together, presenting Rock as 2-0 for the Cook matchup.

TrillerTV lists the rescheduled March 20 broadcast for 8 P.M. Eastern.

item.title: Xania Monet Wins Artist, Song & Album Honors At AI Music Awards
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Xania Monet's path runs from Suno-generated vocals to R&B radio as her creator's project builds on its Hallwood Media deal.
item.content:encoded:
Xania Monet added three trophies to an AI music career that already includes a record deal and a radio breakthrough. The virtual R&B act won artist, song and album of the year at Friday’s AI Music Awards.

The November 13 ceremony at The Mayan was organized by the Sonic Intelligence Academy, which built its voting pool from verified artists in its registry. Members chose nominees and winners by category, with rules barring them from voting for their own work.

Monet’s creator, Telisha “Nikki” Jones, defended the format on the red carpet before the ceremony. “I just feel like AI music is a new thing that people just have to get used to,” Jones told Reuters.

Jones is a Mississippi songwriter who supplies the lyrics while Suno generates music and vocals for the digital performer. Monet’s rise brought a deal with Neil Jacobson’s Hallwood Media and criticism from musicians concerned about replacing human creative work.

That argument was already public in September 2025, when Kehlani challenged the industry’s investment in an artificial R&B act. Kehlani’s objection centered on the labor behind singing, production and songwriting, and the years working artists spend developing those skills.

Monet’s recordings kept reaching listeners, with “How Was I Supposed To Know” entering the Adult R&B Airplay chart at No. 30 in fall 2025. Fifteen reporting stations were playing the track after a 28 percent weekly airplay increase between October 17 and 23.

Before that radio entry, the song had climbed to No. 1 on R&B Digital Song Sales and reached No. 20 on Hot R&B Songs. Monet also appeared on Hot Gospel Songs with “Let Go, Let God,” extending the project beyond its R&B recordings.

The awards program covers 25 categories, including separate prizes for AI-assisted songs and human-and-AI collaborations. Its genre categories also recognize hip-hop, gospel, country, pop and jazz recordings alongside R&B. Monet’s song competed on a ballot that also included Nova Solé, Waking Up Christopher, Millionaire Muses and Aria Blu.

The academy’s staff selects its Off the Charts Spotlight Award rather than the artist voting pool.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Drake’s Stake Case Remains Partly Frozen As Judge Keeps Dismissal Bids Alive
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Drake and Adin Ross can still seek dismissal as a new court order extends the pause in their New Mexico Stake lawsuit.
item.content:encoded:
Drake‘s bid to leave a New Mexico gambling lawsuit remains active even as a federal judge keeps the rest of the Stake case paused. The new order preserves the rapper’s and Adin Ross’s challenges to the court’s authority over them.

Chief U.S. District Judge Kenneth J. Gonzales signed the partial-stay order Friday, November 13. Both sides had requested another 90-day pause while an Illinois case addresses whether Stake-related claims must go through arbitration.

Gonzales left one route open: the pending motions seeking dismissal for lack of personal jurisdiction. Drake and Ross argue that nationally available online content does not establish the New Mexico connections needed to sue them there.

The judge had already allowed those motions to proceed in August. Drake and Ross filed their requests September 7, the plaintiffs responded September 21, and the defendants submitted their reply October 5. Under that August order, discovery and the anticipated arbitration fight remained on hold while those arguments proceeded.

Plaintiffs Nathaniel Torres and Rory Michie allege Stake.us used deceptive promotion to draw them into gambling. Their claims against Drake, Ross and the operator include violations of New Mexico’s Unfair Practices Act and unjust enrichment.

The two men have also sought information about Drake’s Stake payments and promotional reach. They want records showing whether New Mexico residents engaged with the defendants’ content or used their referral links and promotional codes.

In Wednesday’s joint report, lawyers for both sides identified the unresolved arbitration request in Urdan v. Sweepsteaks Limited as the reason to continue waiting. That separate proceeding is pending in the Northern District of Illinois.

“There has not yet been a ruling on the pending motion to compel arbitration in Urdan,” the parties wrote. They said the New Mexico litigation remained in its early stages, despite completed briefing on the jurisdiction dispute.

Gonzales directed the next report to address the future of the pause. “The joint status report shall inform the Court of whether and when the stay shall be fully lifted,” he wrote.

The next joint update is due February 11, 2027, or within 14 days of an Urdan ruling, whichever comes first.

item.title: Wu-Tang Clan’s Rock Hall Night Stays On Track After Nationwide Flight Halt
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Wu-Tang Clan's induction plans survive Friday's travel disruption as Rock Hall confirms its participating artists are in LA.
item.content:encoded:
Wu-Tang Clan‘s Rock & Roll Hall of Fame celebration remains on the calendar after Friday’s nationwide flight halt, with organizers saying the artists needed for the ceremony had already reached Los Angeles.

The timing spared the show a last-minute scramble to get its participants into town. A Rock Hall representative told The Hollywood Reporter that everyone taking part was there and Saturday’s induction was expected to go ahead at the Peacock Theater.

“We’ve been in rehearsals for two days, and the show is going to be incredible and not to be missed,” the representative said.

For Hip-Hop, that assurance protects a night with several generations represented. Wu-Tang enters in the Performer category, while Queen Latifah and MC Lyte receive Early Influence honors. Rick Rubin is among the Musical Excellence recipients, putting another major piece of rap’s recording history in the same class.

Wu-Tang made the cut on its first nomination, alongside first-time nominees Luther Vandross and Phil Collins. The institution requires an act’s first commercial recording to be at least 25 years old before it becomes eligible.

The group’s own story stretches back to Staten Island and an independent single that helped attract Loud Records. Its 1993 debut, Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers), put contrasting voices over RZA’s rough-edged production, with soul samples and martial-arts dialogue woven into the sound.

Saturday also gives Ol’ Dirty Bastard’s family a place in that recognition. His widow, Icelene Jones, said Young Dirty Bastard would represent his father and perform with the group. Jones had arrived in Los Angeles with two of her daughters ahead of the ceremony.

The ceremony also comes one day after the anniversary of ODB’s death. He died on November 13, 2004, at 35, making the family’s appearance both a celebration of Wu-Tang and a remembrance of him.

The travel update concerns the artists participating in the show, not a promise that every inductee will appear. Sade, Oasis and Iron Maiden had already said they would skip the ceremony before Friday’s aviation disruption. Their absences are separate from the flight halt.

The taped ceremony is scheduled to debut on ABC and Disney+ in December.

item.title: Offset Stands By Gunna As Atlanta’s Rap Unity Frays
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Offset keeps Gunna close and argues Atlanta's public splits are costing the city the strength that once made it dominant.
item.content:encoded:
Offset is keeping Gunna in his circle while calling out the divisions he believes have weakened Atlanta rap. His defense puts friendship ahead of the pressure to choose sides after the YSL case.

Speaking on The New York Times’ Popcast, Offset described a relationship built on mutual encouragement. He said Gunna calls him to steer him away from online distractions and back toward music.

“Like end of the day, we friends,” Offset said. He rejected the suggestion that their connection grew out of shared isolation, pointing instead to collaborations that preceded their recent troubles.

Offset argued that Atlanta’s earlier success depended on artists supporting one another despite disagreements. “It’s always politics. You feel me? But we always show unity and we all got on,” he said.

He isn’t just making that argument during an interview. Gunna appears on “Spit Propane,” a song on Offset’s new album, GMFU, released November 13.

Their working relationship had already survived the backlash around Gunna’s December 2022 release from jail. AllHipHop covered their “Prada Dem” collaboration in March 2024, when Offset became Gunna’s first rap feature since that release.

The song arrived after A Gift & a Curse had shown Gunna could still draw a major audience. That 2023 album reached No. 3 on the Billboard 200, while “Fukumean” climbed to No. 8 on the Hot 100.

Gunna left jail after entering an Alford plea to a racketeering conspiracy charge, maintaining his innocence while accepting a negotiated sentence.

He denied cooperating against his co-defendants and did not testify against Young Thug during the trial. The plea nonetheless became a lasting source of tension among his former collaborators.

Lil Baby has approached the same Atlanta tensions differently. In his own recent Popcast appearance, he said any disagreement with Gunna should remain private because a public fight would damage both artists and their city.

That position did not amount to an announced reconciliation. Offset, by contrast, has continued putting his friendship with Gunna into practice through their music together.

Gunna launched SB THE LABEL in October with Atlanta artists Casper Bluff, Nechie and Dracc on its first roster.

item.title: Katt Williams Objects To Faizon Love In “Last Friday” & Jokes About Comedian’s Financial Problems
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Katt Williams gives Ice Cube and Mike Epps two different answers about sharing the next Friday movie with Faizon Love.
item.content:encoded:
Katt Williams brought his issue with Faizon Love up with Ice Cube and Mike Epps during a “Last Friday” casting conversation, then eased his objection before the interview ended.

The November 13 episode of Listen and Laugh brought Williams together with the two hosts to discuss comedy and their movie history. When Epps raised Love’s name, Williams responded by mocking the comedian’s financial troubles.

The talk soon turned to whether Love might have a place in the next “Friday” movie. Williams initially made it sound like the hosts would have to choose.

“Hey, by the way, if you’re in it, I’m not,” Williams said.

Casting has already been a point of discussion for Cube outside this podcast. In a November 11 Club Shay Shay appearance, he said returning characters needed to serve the story rather than show up simply because people wanted to see them again.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Epps described receiving calls from people interested in returning. Cube pointed to the series’ move away from its original neighborhood as an example of why different stories call for different characters.

The production has also taken concrete steps forward. Lawrence Lamont joined as director after making “One Of Them Days,” the Keke Palmer and SZA comedy whose cast included Williams. The franchise has not added a movie since “Friday After Next” in 2002, making this a return after decades away.

Cube and Epps said in Long Beach on July 17 that they had submitted the screenplay. California then included New Line’s “Last Friday” among its October 7 production-tax-credit awards, identifying Cube as the film’s star, writer and producer.

The Southern California production plans to employ more than 180 local cast and crew members.

item.title: Usher Seeks Sanctions In $700K Restaurant Loan Fight
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Usher pushes for court action over a lawyer's disputed answers as his attempt to recover a restaurant loan takes another turn.
item.content:encoded:
Usher wants sanctions against the lawyer handling money for a failed Atlanta restaurant deal, escalating a dispute over the $700,000 he says never came back.

In court documents reviewed by TMZ, the singer accuses Alcide Honore of giving evasive answers about the funds. Usher alleges Honore denied receiving his money, despite wire-transfer records that the singer says establish the payment.

The reported request targets Honore’s conduct during the case; it is not a ruling imposing sanctions. Honore has denied wrongdoing, according to TMZ.

The fight began with plans for Homage ATL, a restaurant proposed for Buckhead. AllHipHop’s November 2025 reporting traced the arrangement to an approach from Bryan Michael Cox the previous year about buying the former Ocean Prime property at 3102 Piedmont Road.

Usher’s complaint said he rejected an ownership investment but agreed to lend $1.7 million in January 2025. The money went into a trust account, with a quick property purchase expected. That distinction put repayment, rather than a share of restaurant profits, at the heart of his claim.

By summer, the purchase still had not happened, according to the lawsuit, and Usher wanted his money returned. He alleged that $1 million came back in August, but the remaining $700,000 did not.

The original complaint also alleged that Honore said returning the balance would be difficult because the funds had gone toward other purposes. The latest reported argument over whether Honore received the money brings the dispute back to documenting where the loan went.

Usher filed the case in Fulton County Superior Court, naming Cox, Keith Thomas and Charles Hughes alongside Honore. Cox’s role made the disagreement especially notable: the producer helped create Usher records including “Burn” and “U Got It Bad.” The two had worked together for more than two decades, including on Confessions, making this a dispute involving an established musical partnership rather than a stranger’s business pitch.

Cox later distanced himself from the transaction, describing himself as a passive minority shareholder without an operational role. He maintained that the business dispute had not broken his 27-year friendship with Usher.

The original suit sought $4.9 million across seven claims, plus attorney fees and litigation costs.

item.title: Will Adam22 Sue Chrisean Rock After “Wild ’N Out” Two-Piece?
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Adam22 is considering legal action after Chrisean Rock socked` him at “Wild ’N Out,” but he me have a difficult time proving real damages.
item.content:encoded:
Adam22 may be shopping for an attorney after his “Wild ’N Out” appearance delivered a punchline he didn’t even write. Pow to the kisser!

The No Jumper founder says he is considering legal action following his confrontation with Chrisean Rock during the November 12 show at Intuit Dome in Inglewood, California. I am sure you all saw it by now. He decided to deliver a rap roast about her parenting. He busted him in the cops with a 2-piece. She left the biscuit though. preceded the physical encounter, and now Adam is questioning whether his jaw can handle his recording schedule.

A comedy booking with a possible consultation afterward? That is an expensive evening out.

According to AllHipHop’s reporting, Adam knew their previous disagreement could become part of the show and deliberately chose to address her parenting. So, he decided go viral in a disgusting way – intentionally. He described the setting as a comedy battle where personal insults were being exchanged. Apparently, they had very different ideas about how the rebuttal portion should work.

Afterward, Adam described swelling and raised concerns about how much talking his livelihood requires. I did not see it from the video.

“I have to talk on camera oftentimes for like four, five, six, seven hours in a day, right? So, her rocking my jaw is actually something that could kind of take me out of work for a significant period of time,” Adam22 said.

His concerns about lost work remain his own assessment. I think he may be able to press a charge.

And before anybody starts assigning courtroom seats, AllHipHop’s report did not establish that he had filed a lawsuit or police report. Considering legal action and actually filing are different developments. Meh. These people are weird. And “Wild ’N Out” is definitely on a different type of time at this point in their decades-old history.

Will Adam pursue the matter beyond his camera?

Hip-Hop needs a purge, if this is even Hip-Hop.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Fat Joe’sEx-Hypeman Seeks Free Lawyer To Fight Defamation Case
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Fat Joe's former collaborator asks the court for volunteer counsel as he prepares a bid to end the defamation suit.
item.content:encoded:
Fat Joe‘s former hypeman wants a volunteer lawyer to help him seek judgment without a trial in the rapper’s defamation lawsuit.

Terrance Dixon submitted the request ahead of a November 13 deadline to address his representation after Tyrone Blackburn left his legal team.

The request follows Judge Jennifer E. Willis’ October 2 decision allowing Blackburn to withdraw from Dixon’s two linked cases. Her order offered Dixon three choices: hire another lawyer, represent himself or request volunteer counsel.

In a November 12 application filed in Manhattan federal court, Dixon outlined his next move against his former boss. He also submitted a separate application asking to proceed without prepaying court fees or costs.

“I need an attorney because discovery has ended and I want to move for summary judgment,” Dixon wrote. “I have not yet asked for an attorney in this case because I was previously represented by Tyrone Blackburn, who is also a defendant in this case. However, he withdrew and the court gave until Nov. 13 for me to find another attorney or submit an application for pro bono counsel.”

Dixon said he had sought assistance from the City Bar Justice Center’s Pro Se Clinic. He described a limit on the help it could provide for the motion he wants to file.

“I have contacted the Pro Se Clinic at the City Bar Justice Center and have had calls about my case and next steps with them,” Dixon wrote. “They stated that they did not have the resources to assist me in drafting my motion for summary judgment and usually only help plaintiffs oppose summary judgment. They have assisted me in filling out this application.”

Fat Joe sued Dixon and Blackburn in April 2025, alleging they tried to extract money through false accusations. Dixon later brought his own lawsuit alleging abuse and unpaid work, claims the rapper denied.

Blackburn’s withdrawal did not remove him as a defendant or end the court’s authority over pending sanctions matters. The October order paused issues involving Dixon through November 13.

Even if the court approves Dixon’s request, an attorney must volunteer to take the case.

item.title: Archie Eversole’s Brother Sees Murder Charges Dropped Days Before Trial
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Archie Eversole's brother avoids a murder trial as prosecutors say their latest review cannot support a conviction.
item.content:encoded:
Archie Eversole‘s brother will no longer face a murder trial over the Atlanta rapper’s death, ending a prosecution that stretched more than four years and was headed toward a courtroom next week.

Alexander Krause, 46, had been awaiting trial on charges stemming from the 2022 shooting. The DeKalb County District Attorney’s Office announced Friday that it was dropping every count because prosecutors could not establish his guilt beyond a reasonable doubt, according to WSB-TV’s reporting.

“Our decision in this matter reflects our commitment to justice, fairness, and transparency,” the DA’s office said.

A review undertaken as prosecutors prepared for trial changed their assessment of the evidence. The office said investigators found no evidence of a dispute between the brothers, while messages recovered from Eversole’s phone supported accounts that they had a good relationship.

The DA’s office also described limits to what forensic testing established. Prosecutors said a weapon the brothers jointly owned contained DNA from both men, and the evidence did not eliminate the reasonable possibility of a self-inflicted injury.

The dismissal follows an April 2023 indictment charging Krause with malice murder, felony murder, aggravated assault and a firearm offense. He had been released on bond in August 2022 while the case remained pending.

Questions about identification were part of the proceedings long before Friday’s announcement. Prosecutors previously said Eversole made statements pointing to his brother, but defense attorney David Schnipper disputed that account and argued that Eversole never identified Krause as the shooter.

Eversole was wounded on March 25, 2022, at the home he shared with his brother and sought help at a nearby gas station. He later died in the hospital at 37.

His music had already become part of Atlanta’s sports culture. “We Ready,” recorded with Bubba Sparxxx, became a stadium staple, and Atlanta United embraced the track as part of its match-day atmosphere.

The club publicly mourned Eversole after his death, remembering an artist who supported the team before its inaugural season. His connection to its supporters extended well beyond the song’s original release.

Prosecutors prepared a nolle prosequi order to dismiss all charges.
